events.title: Node.js first released
events.summary: Ryan Dahl released Node.js on May 27, 2009 — server-side JavaScript on Google's V8 with an event loop.
events.about: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser for APIs, CLIs, and real-time servers. Its non-blocking I/O model powers npm's ecosystem — Express, NestJS, webpack, and millions of packages. Example: a chat server handling thousands of WebSocket connections on one thread via callbacks and later async/await.

narrative.whyChosen: Node made JavaScript a full-stack language and reshaped how teams build web backends.
narrative.whyImportant: V8 plus an event loop proved JS could handle I/O-bound servers at scale, not just browser UI.
narrative.problemSolved: Server frameworks blocked on each request; Dahl wanted C10k-style concurrency with a language front-end devs already knew.
